title: RAG at scale: production ready GenAI apps with Azure AI Search
talk_summary: A Microsoft Azure AI Search PM walks through the retrieval half of RAG at production scale: two-stage recall-then-rerank, hybrid vector+keyword fusion, quantization, and managed incremental ingestion. It is mostly a product tour of Azure AI Search, but a few retrieval-quality mechanisms are copyable.

takeaways.technique: Two-stage retrieval: cheap recall then cross-encoder rerank
takeaways.what_they_do: First stage pulls many candidates with fast vector/keyword recall; second stage runs a heavier cross-encoder over only that small set to rerank for quality.
takeaways.numbers: reranker ~100ms; better results across the board vs keyword-only, vector-only, and fusion

takeaways.technique: Hybrid fusion of keyword + vector with separate candidate vs return counts
takeaways.what_they_do: Query both BM25-style keyword and vector indexes, fuse results, and decouple how many candidates each side retrieves from how many are returned.
takeaways.evidence_quote: separate how many candidates you want from how many you want to return

takeaways.what_they_do: Narrow the candidate set with discrete metadata filters first, then apply ranking tricks on the smaller set.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you know discrete um metadata elements that can help you narrow the data set that's the most effective way
takeaways.numbers: filters fine even at hundreds of millions of documents

takeaways.technique: Vector quantization with full-precision oversampling + rerank
takeaways.what_they_do: Store compressed (int8/1-bit) vectors for fast recall, keep full-precision copies to rerank oversampled candidates, trading a little quality for big density/speed gains.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can get the Precision remaining Precision back by reranking

takeaways.what_they_do: A set-up-once pipeline tracks source changes, reprocesses only deltas, handles formats/chunking/vectorization, so cost is incremental.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we only in process the changes so the cost is also incremental
